Further our cat which was clearly emaciated was declared to be of healthy weight by her that day. Had she alerted us about his frailness (which is her literal job as a doctor), we could have done something. Our cat came back, and we noticed his reducing appetite day by day. That day was one of the worst days in our baby’s life. He pooped continuously to the point when even blood came out and he suffered from severe diarrhoea. When Dr Prachi was informed of this in a state of panic, she prescribed an antibiotic and asked us to take him to Vetic if there is an emergency. The next morning, our baby was slowly breathing in the morning and was limp, we rushed to Vetic and met Dr Teja (who is a gem of a person; tried to save Tinu but couldn’t). After successive days of continuous IV medication, he even started to get better and started becoming responsive. If this doctor is not an expert, she could have let us know earlier. And we would have taken our cat to another doctor. But she didn’t do that. Her carelessness costed our baby his life. Would ask her to introspect the consequences of her actions.
